synthesis:draft.headline: Forecast vs actual in SA1: one large under‑forecast observed at 2026-07-31 13:00 ACST
summary: Comparison run matched POE50 forecasts to OPERATIONAL_DEMAND actuals for 48 matched pairs (evidence: ev1171).
Mean absolute error (MAE) over the compared pairs was 72.88 MW (evidence: ev1169).
Mean signed error (POE50 − actual) over the compared pairs was 8.12 MW (evidence: ev1170).
The largest absolute error was POE50 − actual = −292.0 MW at 2026-07-31 13:00 ACST (error percent −26.72%) (evidence: ev1159, ev1160).
For the interval near the supplied event_peak_interval_end (2026-07-30 16:30 ACST) the forecast error was +50.0 MW (POE50 − actual = 50.0 MW) (evidence: ev1071).
Observed actual operational demand peak in the retrieved series: 2173.0 MW at 2026-07-30 19:00 ACST (evidence: ev0010).
Tooling note: the formal forecast-vs-actual comparison was computed on a 24‑hour constrained window (48 pairs, ev1171); see uncertainties for the excluded final half‑hour.

possible_explanations.statement: The large negative error at 2026-07-31 13:00 ACST may reflect unexpected local generation shortfall or unit unavailability.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Check unit availability and outage records for SA1 for 2026-07-31 12:30–13:30 ACST and compare scheduled generation to actual dispatch.

possible_explanations.statement: The large negative error might be associated with atypical interconnector flows affecting net local demand.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Retrieve NETINTERCHANGE / interconnector dispatch for SA1 for 2026-07-31 12:30–13:30 ACST to see if imports/exports differed materially from forecasts.

possible_explanations.statement: The large negative error could be driven by a rapid weather-driven demand change.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Fetch SA1 weather observations (temperature, wind, cloud) for the hours around 2026-07-31 12:00–14:00 ACST and compare to forecast weather used by demand models.
